title: PCR Prep from cDNA for IVT Reactions

steps_raw.instruction: PCR Prep from cDNA for IVT Reactions

Scope and Applicability: PCR1 and PCR2 reactions beginning with cDNA to generate transcript templates ready for IVT reaction. This protocol is written for 192 (2x96) reactions but can also be used for fewer or more reactions by adjusting the amount of materials and equipment appropriately.
cDNA, stored at -20ºC.
Forward and Reverse-SP6 Primers (IDT or ABA) at 10 µM each at -20ºC.
Forward and Nested-SP6 Primers (IDT or ABA) at 10 µM each at -20ºC.
Qiagen Taq PCR Master Mix (Qiagen 201445) at 4ºC.
Nuclease-free water (NF dH2O). (Ambion 9932 or equivalent).
Kimwipes (Kimtech 34256)
96-well PCR plate (x8) (Genesee 96-well Full Skirt Plate 22-319)
96-well Millipore Montage filter plate (x2) (Millipore MANU03050)
96-well BD Falcon UV plate (x2) (BD Falcon Microplates 353261)
96-well V-bottom (x2) (VWR 47743-996)
96-well rubber mat (x2) (ABI)
Rainin Single Pipetteman (p2, p200, p1000)
Rainin 12-channel Pipetteman (p10, p20, p200)
Electronic 8-channel Pipetteman (p20, p200)
Filter tips (p10, p200, p1000)
25 ml reagent reservoir (x4) (VWR 41428954)
Thermalcycler (MJ or BioRad)
Bench-top centrifuge for spinning down 96-well plates (Eppendorf 5810 R)
Millipore 96well vacuum manifold and vacuum pump with regulator and trap
SpectraMax M2 (Spectrophotometer)
Wear latex or nitrile gloves throughout protocol to prevent RNase contamination.
Glycerol stocks contain E.coli, dispose of pipette tips in broken glass container.
Purified ds PCR2 product ready for IVT reaction.
MB0004: 2100 Bioanalyzer Operation for PCR, GTP, and IVT Products
https://www.protocols.io/view/2100-bioanalyzer-operation-for-pcr-gtp-and-ivt-pro-bfzjjp4n

Warning: This protocol is extremely sensitive to RNase contamination; ensure that you have been properly trained using sterile techniques before starting this protocol. Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.

NOTE: unless otherwise noted, ‘spin down’ means to spin the tubes in a microcentrifuge for 5-10” at top speed (or plates in the bench-top centrifuge for 2’ at 1800rpm) in order to drive the liquid to the bottom of the tube/wells.
This protocol is meant for x2 plates of 96 PCR reactions each:
24 hours before planned PCR reaction, make sure there is enough Taq PCR Master Mix (1.7 ml bottles) at 4ºC.
If more is needed, transfer a box from -20ºC to 4ºC to thaw O/N.
Do not use master mix that has been at 4ºC longer than 1 month.
24 hours before planned PCR reaction, transfer 10 µM primer plates (Forward, Reverse and Nested) from -20ºC to 4ºC.
Day of reaction transfer glycerol stock plates from -80ºC to RT:
Allow 1.5 hr for 384-well plates to thaw.
Allow 1.0 hr for 96-well plates to thaw.
Remove Taq PCR Master Mix from 4ºC and place in a bench-top cooler.
Label 96-well PCR plate as “PCR_YYMMDD_PP” where YY=year, MM=month, DD=day, PP=plate#.
Remove primer plates from 4ºC to RT and spread out to continue thawing.
Methodology/Procedures:
Thaw cDNA (from -20ºC) at RT for 10’.
Make cDNA/nuclease-free water premix. Adjust volumes for number of samples with 10% overage.
Vortex premix for 5” and store in bench-top cooler.
Add other reaction components as shown in the table below:
Vortex Taq MasterMix for 5”, spin down.
Pipette MM into reagent reservoir.
Aliquot 25 µl of Taq MM to plates with electronic 8-channel p200 repeater with filter tips.
Pour cDNA/nuclease-free water premix into reagent reservoir.
Aliquot 20 µl cDNA premix with electronic 8-channel p200 repeater with filter tips.
Spin down primer plates.
Add 2.5 µl of 10 µM each For and Rev primers using 12-channel p10 with filter tips or add 5 µl of 10 µM combined FOR/REV primers.
Spin down PCR plates.
Using BioRad (Thermo) or MJ Thermalcycler, run the PCR through the following cycles:

Return the leftover Taq PCR Master Mix (date and “X” the tube) to 4ºC and return primer plates to 4ºC. Keep these primer plates at 4ºC until the PCR2 plate has successfully gone through UV Quantification and the PCR has been confirmed to have worked.
When the cycling is finished (2.5 hr), spin down the plates.
Run a spot check of 12 samples (6 samples/plate) on the Bioanalyzer (see MB0004).
Seal plates with plate mat and store at 4ºC if moving on to PCR2 reaction within 24 hours. Otherwise, seal plates and store at -20ºC until needed for PCR2 reaction
PCR2 from PCR1 template:
Prepare and add reaction components as shown in the table below:
Bring template to appropriate concentration:
If using PCR1: 1 µl of PCR1 into 99 µl of nuclease-free water.
If using from RA plate: 3.0 µl of PCR1 RA (1:10) into 27 µl nuclease-free water.
Vortex Taq PCR Master Mix for 5” and spin down.
Pipette Taq PCR Master Mix into a 25 ml reagent reservoir.
Aliquot 25 µl of Taq PCR Master Mix to plates using electronic 8-channel p200 with filter tips.
Pour approximately 4 ml of nuclease-free water into a 25 ml reagent reservoir.
Aliquot 19 µl nuclease-free water to PCR plates using electronic 8-channel p200 with filter tips.
Aliquot 1 µl of 1:100 PCR1 template with 12-channel p10 with filter tips.
Spin down primer plates.
Add 2.5 µl of 10 µM each FOR and NEST primers using 12-channel p10 with filter tips or add 5 µl of 10 µM combined FOR/NEST primers.
Spin down PCR plates.
Using BioRad (Thermo) or MJ Thermalcycler, run the PCR through the following cycles making sure that the blocks are at 95C before inserting plates (hot start protocol):

Return the leftover Taq PCR Master Mix (date and “X” the tube) to 4ºC and return primer plates to 4ºC. Keep these primer plates at 4ºC until the PCR plate has successfully gone through UV Quantification and the PCR has been confirmed to have worked.
When the cycling is finished (2.5 hr), spin down the plates.
Run a spot check of 12 samples (6 samples/plate) on the Bioanalyzer (see MB0004).
Clean-up/Purification:
Check to make sure lines and trap of vacuum are hooked up correctly.
Label Montage-96 filter plate with PCR plate number.
Seal any unused wells with aluminum tape.
Fill 25 ml reagent reservoir with approx. 30 ml of nuclease-free water.

Using 12-channel p200 with filter tips, add 55 µl of nuclease-free water to a row, mix up and down two times, then transfer all 105 µl to filter plate (takes two transfers). Do this with each row in the plate changing tips each time.

Once all samples have been transferred to filter plate, place Montage-96 plate without lid on vacuum manifold. Turn on vacuum, press plate down on manifold and verify that the vacuum pressure reaches 20-22” mm Hg.
Set timer for 5 minutes.
Fill a 25 ml reservoir with approximately 11 ml of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0.
Shut vacuum off after 5 minutes (filters should look shiny, have no liquid), let vacuum release on its own (i.e. don’t pull plate off manifold).
Fold Kimwipe and blot underside of plate onto towel.
Add 50 µl of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to each row using 12-channel p200 with filter tips, changing tips between each row.
Place lid on filter plate. Let samples incubate at RT for 30 minutes for resuspension.
Label the following plates for each reaction set. Initial and date each.
V-bottom 96-well plate: “PCR2plateID_M”
96-well PCR plate: “PCR2plateID, BA 1:2”
UV 96-well plate with “PCR2plateID UV”

After 30 minutes, recover 50 µl (actual volume will be between 45-50 µl) of sample from filters into the labeled V-bottom 96 plate using 12-channel p200 with filter tips. Pipette up and down twice to mix sample across filter before recovering. Change tips between each row.
Make Bioanalyzer (BA) at 1:2 dilution and UV at 1:25 dilution aliquot plates:
Add 4.0 µl of nuclease-free water to BA plate, using electronic 8-channel p20 repeater with filter tips (not necessary to change tips), from nuclease-free water reservoir.
Transfer 4.0 µl of PCR sample to UV then BA plates (two transfers from each row), using 12-channel p10 with filter tips.
Add 96 µl of nuclease-free water to UV plate, using 12-channel p200 with filter tips. Change tips between each row. Adding 96 µl water after sample ensures good mixing.
Seal PCR2 plate and BA plate with plate sealer, store in -20ºC.
Seal UV plates with aluminum tape and spin down.

Take UV plates to SpectraMax M2, choose “DNA_bkgd_constant-PCR_Falcon_110817 or DNA _bkgd_constant-PCR_Costar_110817110817” from Assays menu. Save file as “PCRplateID_date” to the location of your choice. Click Read. While the Plate section is highlighted, choose Import Plate from the Plate menu and import the appropriate text file for that PCR2plateID. Save the file after the data is in. Repeat for the second plate.
Store UV plates at 4ºC, sealed with aluminum tape.
Remove BA plate from -20ºC and thaw for 3 minutes and spin down.
Run samples in BA plate on Bioanalyzer (see MB0004).
If sample concentrations are between 50-100 ng/µl, then OK to move primer plates to -20ºC.
Store left-over Taq PCR Master Mix reagents at 4ºC.
Return bench-top cooler to -20ºC.
PCR and BA plates stored at -20ºC.
UV plates stored at 4ºC
Technical Information:
Montage filter plates are size exclusion filter plates and will only let very small (<100bp) molecules through. The PCR product is recovered on top of the filter, primers are filtered through.
